title: Geofencing design decisions and developer checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for engineers and oncall about a thin, operationally-friendly geofencing approach for customer region commitments (what we previously called ‘pinning’). Focus: pragmatic developer workflows, low-risk enforcement, and a measurable telemetry surface for migration and rollouts.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Private and Dedicated customers that require traffic locality guarantees (data-in-region). Hosted product has separate flow.
- We assume customers may request strict residency (all inference and logs stay in-region) or soft residency (in-region preference with permitted controlled fallbacks).
- This doc intentionally focuses on runtime routing + developer integration points, not legal contract wording.

Short summary of recommended approach (TL;DR):
1) Abstraction: Add a lightweight request attribute "geo_policy" that can be set to: required | preferred | unrestricted.
2) Router semantics: 
   - required: route only to nodes with matching region tag; reject (403-like) if none available unless an explicit operator override is used.
   - preferred: attempt region-local routing with a timeboxed retry/fallback to cross-region pool if SLOs at risk.
   - unrestricted: normal routing.
3) Developer checklist and simple SDK flags so app teams can opt-in per-route.
4) Telemetry: emit residency_decision events with fields (requested, chosen_region, fallback, latency_ms, cost_delta_est).

Design alternatives considered (notes):
- Strict per-customer pinned clusters: simplest guarantees but high cost (dedicated capacity blowups, low utilization). Rejected as default.
- Network-level enforcement (VPC-only egress controls): good for on-prem/HSM, but adds ops friction and fragile for multi-cloud. Useful as an optional layer.
- Tag-based soft routing (our recommendation): balances cost and reliability; supports graceful fallbacks.

Developer checklist (for service owners integrating residency):
- API surface: add header or SDK param: X-Redwood-Geo-Policy: required|preferred|unrestricted. Document default is preferred for new endpoints.
- Config: annotate routes in service config with residency: {policy: preferred, allowed_regions: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]}
- Error handling: explicitly handle 4xx residency errors. User-facing messages must not leak infra details; use: "Region temporarily unavailable: try again or contact support".
- Fallback plan: implement exponential backoff + optional user-visible fallback consent flow (if applicable to product).
- Tests: include unit tests that simulate no-local-capacity and assert telemetry events emitted; integration tests exercising affinity routing under CHAOS.
- Rollout: start as feature-flagged behavior for a single service, run 2 weeks with telemetry; then scale to more routes.

Routing semantics and implementation notes for engineers:
- Router will evaluate (in order): 1) explicit allowed_regions on the request 2) geo_policy header 3) customer-account default residency setting.
- Candidate node selection: prefer nodes with matching region tag and healthy connection pool. Use weighted scoring: health(50) + locality_match(30) + recent_latency_percentile(20).
- Timeboxed fallback window for preferred: 150ms by default for low-latency customers, 300ms for best-effort. Configurable per-customer.
- Fallback must compute an estimated cost delta (approx tokens * per-token delta) and attach to telemetry so sales/CS can evaluate pricing impacts.

Telemetry / observability (MUST):
- residency_decision event: fields as strings/numbers: request_id, customer_id, requested_policy, selected_region, fallback_taken (true/false), fallback_reason, latency_ms, cost_delta_est, node_tags, timestamp
- Expose a dashboard: % requests honored by policy (by customer), average fallback latency, top fallback reasons.
- Add a slow-path alarm: if % preferred->fallback > 5% in 1h for a customer, trigger paging for the account SRE/AE.

Security and audit considerations:
- When policy=required, rejections must be auditable (persist rejection records with operator id if override used).
- KMS/HSM: ensure encryption-of-logs config respects residency; redact any KMS key ids in public logs.

Operator tooling & emergency overrides:
- Admin console toggle: allow temporary override for a customer to bypass residency for X minutes with mandatory incident note. Override should be auditable with who/why/expiry.
- CLI: rwdctl residency-override --account <acct> --until <ISO> --reason "maintenance" --actor <name>
- Emergency rollback: if a region suffers an outage, automatically move customers with preferred policy to fallback pools but mark all requests with fallback_reason=region_unavailable.

Migration and rollout plan (developer + ops playbook):
- Phase 0: Internal canary - pick a non-critical service, enable telemetry only, collect baseline. (2 weeks)
- Phase 1: Preferred opt-in for a small customer cohort; monitor fallback rate and latency impact. (2-4 weeks)
- Phase 2: Harden required path for customers who bought strict residency - run full acceptance tests, legal signoff. (4-6 weeks)
- Phase 3: Default preference shift for new routes to preferred. Documented in SDK and quickstarts. (ongoing)

QA and chaos testing checklist:
- Simulate regional node drain during high RPS and verify preferred fallback window behavior.
- Inject tag-mismatch and assert required policy causes clear rejections and admin override path works.
- Telemetry verification: assert residency_decision events contain populated cost_delta_est values across test scenarios.

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- What is the canonical costing model for cost_delta_est? (cc: finance) Need a simple per-token or per-GB estimate mapping. ACTION: Finance to propose a baseline by 2025-01-31.
- How to encode multi-region affinity for customers that want EU+UK but not US? Schema proposal: allowed_regions as a set (done) but need UI affordance in Console. UX needs design.
- Legal: when do we log a fallback as an incident for contract breach? Is a single fallback tolerated? ACTION: Legal to define thresholds.
- Should we expose customer-visible metadata when a fallback occurs? Risk of exposing infra topology. Proposal: only show high-level messages; expose more detail in account activity logs accessible to AEs.

Appendix: sample config snippet (YAML-like)

route: /v1/generate
residency:
  policy: preferred
  allowed_regions: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]
  fallback_window_ms: 200

SDK example (pseudo):
client.generate(prompt, {geoPolicy: 'required', allowedRegions: ['eu-west-1']})

Action items (owners):
- Define cost_delta_est algorithm (Finance + Applied-ML) - Marta (due 2025-01-31)
- Implement residency_decision telemetry schema + dashboard - DevInfra (Jon) (due 2025-02-10)
- Add SDK header support and quickstart docs - DevX (Devon) (due 2025-01-20)
- Design Console UI for allowed_regions - Product (PM TBD) (discuss in Jan roadmap)

Notes to self / messy/thought fragments: 
- Might be useful to add a "graceful degradation" response that returns a short explanation and an id for support lookup.
- Consider combining with cookie-based prefix caching to avoid cross-region retransmits for repeated requests.
- Keep admin override timeboxed and require a postmortem for overrides longer than 4 hours.
- This approach should avoid the need for per-customer dedicated clusters 90% of the time.

References and related tickets:
- CONFLUENCE-1421: Geofencing requirements (draft)
- JIRA-RDW-5472: Residency telemetry schema
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-config/pull/389

End of doc.
